Hi Avery / team — attaching the per-feature econ CSV + short scenario math below. I kept the model intentionally simple so procurement can follow the line items quickly. Attachment: redwood-per-feature-econ-1m-token-model.csv

Assumptions (base):
- tokens_per_feature = 1,200
- baseline_features_per_month = 50,000
- peak_features_per_month = 200,000
- ARPU (HealthSync stated) = $120 ARR per paid account (=> $10/mo)

Per-feature cost (direct inference cost) at several price points (simple formula: cost_per_feature = price_per_1M * (tokens_per_feature / 1_000_000)):
- price $6 / 1M => cost_per_feature = 6 * 0.0012 = $0.0072 (~$0.72 cents)
- price $10 / 1M => cost_per_feature = 10 * 0.0012 = $0.012 (1.2 cents)
- price $14 / 1M => cost_per_feature = 14 * 0.0012 = $0.0168 (1.68 cents)

Monthly spend (baseline 50k):
- $6/1M => 50,000 * $0.0072 = $360/mo
- $10/1M => 50,000 * $0.012 = $600/mo
- $14/1M => 50,000 * $0.0168 = $840/mo

Monthly spend (peak 200k): multiply above by 4 => $1,440 / $2,400 / $3,360 respectively.

Per-user annualized inference load examples (to get to CAC payback):
- Low-adoption user: 10 feature calls/mo => 120 calls/yr => tokens/year = 144,000 => 0.144M tokens/yr
- High-adoption user: 40 feature calls/mo => 480 calls/yr => tokens/year = 576,000 => 0.576M tokens/yr

Annual inference cost per user (at $10/1M):
- Low: 0.144M * $10 = $1.44 / year (~$0.12/mo)
- High: 0.576M * $10 = $5.76 / year (~$0.48/mo)

Example CAC payback math (simple contribution margin approach):
- Use ARPU = $120/yr => $10/mo revenue per paying account.
- Subtract inference cost to get gross contribution from the feature (we assume other marginal costs negligible for this exercise).

Contribution per month (at $10/1M):
- Low usage user: revenue $10.00 - inference cost $0.12 = $9.88 contribution/mo
- High usage user: revenue $10.00 - inference cost $0.48 = $9.52 contribution/mo

If CAC = $120 (conservative band):
- Low usage payback = 120 / 9.88 ≈ 12.1 months
- High usage payback = 120 / 9.52 ≈ 12.6 months

If CAC = $60 (aggressive band):
- Low usage payback = 60 / 9.88 ≈ 6.1 months
- High usage payback = 60 / 9.52 ≈ 6.3 months

Notes / implications:
- The inference cost per user is small relative to ARPU, so payback is primarily driven by CAC + adoption. Keeping price near $10/1M yields predictable sub-dollar per-user annual inference cost at the usage levels we discussed.
- If HealthSync wants sub-12 month payback under the conservative CAC ($120), you either need to drive lower CAC (marketing/sales improvements), increase ARPU (feature monetization), or reduce per-1M price via a committed band (we can show 10–25% discounts at 12-month reserved commits).

Requested artifacts delivered:
- Attached CSV (redwood-per-feature-econ-1m-token-model.csv) with scenario toggles (tokens per call, price per 1M, baseline/peak volumes)
- One-page executive summary: (attached as top of CSV / first sheet) — short bullet conclusions + recommended committed discount band to meet sub-12 month payback at conservative CAC.

3) Tech/implementation: if you confirm baseline, we’ll spin a pilot key and capture token telemetry to validate the 1,200 token assumption in week 1.
